Figure_1.title: Learning makes measured reagent swaps useful beyond their original recipe
Figure_1.legend: **A**, Replacing PdCl₂(dtbpf) with PdCl₂(PPh₃)₂ raises the Suzuki yield of 6-bromoquinoline from 5% to 93% but lowers that of 5-bromo-1H-indazole from 84% to 12%. Across nineteen arrays, 271/283 testable substitutions contradict independent substrate-pair and background signs (Fig. 2). **B**, Copying and learning receive the same two reference wells for the target substrate pair in another recipe. Copying transfers their yield difference; learning relates their difference and mean yield to the target through historical reactions. Across seventeen screens, mean squared error changes by +42.4% with copying and −13.7% with learning relative to history alone (Fig. 3A). Grey labels locate prior work at recommendation, historical learning and general-condition selection; the unlabelled fork tests how to reuse the same measurement. **C**, Moving methylthio from meta to para on an aniline defeats the HBTU recipe; TPTU restores 93% yield (Fig. 4A). Measured alternatives resolve 285/542 shared-scope conflicts (Fig. 4C).

Figure_2.title: Substitution responses depend jointly on substrate and recipe background
Figure_2.legend: **A**, Responses to PdCl₂(dtbpf) → PdCl₂(PPh₃)₂ for 412 substrate pairs measured under both Cs₂CO₃ and K₂CO₃; 145 have opposite signs (shaded quadrants; Pearson r = 0.55). A 2 × 2 matrix shows the responses for 5-bromo-1H-indazole and 2-bromo-3-methoxypyridine under the two carbonates; matching numbers identify the corresponding scatter points. The three negative responses and one positive response cannot all be reproduced by multiplying one sign per substrate pair by one sign per background. **B**, Each atlas row gives an array, the number of measured substrate pairs (n), the complete response distribution for one exact substitution, and conflicting/testable swap counts using all nonzero changes or changes of at least 20 points. Each array uses its most measured substitution, except Suzuki, which retains the flagship catalyst substitution. All nineteen selected substitutions contain positive (blue) and negative (red) responses; exact zeros are grey. Totals are 271/283 and 143/212. A swap is testable when its observed pair-background graph contains a cycle.

Figure_3.title: Historical relationships make the same reference measurements useful
Figure_3.legend: **A**, Two reference wells measured for the target substrate pair in another recipe background (top) are either copied or related to the target through historical reactions. Prediction-error changes relative to history alone are shown for seventeen screens and the hierarchical group average (Overall); screens are ordered by learned error change. Overall changes are +42.4% for copying and −13.7% for learning. The arrow marks a copied-error value beyond the plotted range. The inset counts missed or wrong directions among 21,997 held-out changes of at least 20 points: 18.6 per hundred for copying and 13.6 for learning; zero predictions count as missed directions. **B**, Reference and target responses for 452 training pairs in an amide-coupling additive substitution, pentafluorophenol → N-hydroxyphthalimide. The orange line copies at unit slope; the teal line shows the learned predictor at mean reference activity. **C**, Error removed by a reference for the same substitution relative to a matched control substitution. Grey points denote screens and teal points hierarchical group averages; rows give the held-out object and the fraction of historical training data (25% or 100%). Orange denotes copying and teal learning.

Figure_4.title: Measured alternatives resolve part of the shared-scope conflict
Figure_4.legend: **A,B**, Each example follows a structural change, failure of the original recipe (red outline) and restoration by a measured alternative (blue outline). Halos mark the relocated groups. **A**, Moving methylthio from meta to para lowers the HBTU/no-HOBt amide yield from 91% to 0%; TPTU without HOBt gives 93% for the para isomer with the same phenoxyacetic acid. The network joins recipes differing in one slot, with DIPEA, DMF, 25 °C and 2 h fixed. **B**, Twelve Suzuki yields before and after boronic-acid methyl relocation with the same bromoindazole. Under K₃PO₄, PdCl₂(PCy₃)₂ falls from 48% to 0%; SPhos Pd G3 gives 92% after relocation. **C**, Shared-scope conflicts resolved by measured alternatives in each transformation: 285 of 542 overall, with 257 unresolved. Within the resolved subset, 266, 16 and 3 conflicts require one, two and three additional options.

Figure_S1.title: Exact substitutions span nineteen reaction arrays
Figure_S1.legend: Bars give exact substitution counts for nineteen non-Finkelstein arrays. Bar-end numbers count substitutions; the right column counts distinct substrate pairs within each array. Counts of pairs are not additive across arrays. The retained source corpus contains 410,587 records in twenty tables after 396 exclusions; the nineteen arrays shown contain 406,909 records.

Figure_S8.title: Local profiles and historical reactions provide complementary information
Figure_S8.legend: **a**, Original local-update curves for the fixed common16 population of 22,963 queries supporting sixteen local profiles. Budgets are 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 profiles; values show error changes relative to history alone. Local-only and history-plus-local curves retain the original equal-group, edge-balanced weighting and historical reference. **b**, The separate fixed common8 population contains 24,221 queries supporting eight local profiles. Adding history is compared with profiles alone at the same budgets of 1, 2, 4 and 8 profiles; eight profiles lower error by 9.7%. For both panels, the horizontal axis gives profile counts and the minimum–maximum number of endpoint wells. One profile contains two reagent endpoints in each included recipe background. The populations and baselines differ between panels; all values use existing predictions without model refitting.

Figure_S3.title: Calibration between libraries usually worsens the target-only baseline
Figure_S3.legend: All seventeen fixed-support, scored transfers between libraries. Each line follows one direction from target-only prediction to calibrated transfer and the source-identity reassignment control. Errors are normalized to the target-only error for that direction. Calibration worsens fifteen directions (red) and improves two (teal). The source difference channel, budget of 192 and fixed target support follow the original cross-library analysis.

Figure_S6.title: Structure-based prediction primarily recovers each pair's own response level
Figure_S6.legend: This structure-only task excludes both partner molecules from training and is distinct from the two-reference-well learning task in Figure 3. **a**, Two measured response vectors from the substitution with the most supported complete vectors in the three-group decomposition; the displayed pairs have the minimum and maximum own mean response within that population. Solid lines show responses across backgrounds; dashed lines show each pair's own mean. **b**, Error removed within each layer, divided by that layer's centroid-baseline error, for the three-group, group-and-edge-balanced comparison. Approximately 5.0% of pair-level error and 0.22% of background-fluctuation error are removed. **c**, Pair-level (blue) and fluctuation (teal) contributions to net total improvement for two or three groups and three weightings. Each pair's own level accounts for 91.1–96.6% of net improvement. This share uses a different denominator from panel b.

Figure_S4.title: A representative matched-reference comparison illustrates direction and magnitude separately
Figure_S4.legend: **a**, Replacing PdCl₂(dtbpf) with XPhos Pd G3 gives opposite responses in the K₃PO₄ reference and Cs₂CO₃ target backgrounds of the same substrate pair. Target wells were withheld from prediction. **b**, Copying predicts −10.5 percentage points, learning +5.6 points and the measured target change is +34.4 points. Learning identifies the direction but underestimates its magnitude. The predeclared rule requires a reference change of at least 10 points, a measured target change of at least 20 points, an incorrect copied sign and a correct learned sign, plus four retained measured endpoints. The nested eligible pools contain zero flagship-catalyst, 136 Suzuki and 529 total comparisons. The selected Suzuki comparison is nearest the median absolute learned error; lexical identities resolve ties.

Figure_S2.title: Additional molecular changes reshape reagent preferences
Figure_S2.legend: **a**, All sixteen measured yields for acid fluorination and two anilines. Activator and additive are each 1.5 equiv in DMF at 25 °C for 2 h, without base. **b**, FDPP-to-TOTU response contrasts between primary aryl and primary alkyl amines within 42 common acid partners; the red line marks their mean of 33.87 pp. **c**, NMM-to-DIPEA difference-in-differences: the response for 4-methoxybenzylamine minus that for benzylamine over the same eight acids. Points are acids and red ticks their means.

Figure_S5.title: Measured response differences and local information contribute differently
Figure_S5.legend: **a**, Information added by the observed reference difference D beyond mean reference activity S, expressed as the intended-swap improvement minus the matched different-swap improvement in each screen. The pair-held-out, full-history, context-balanced complete-panel population is retained. **b**, Fixed-operator label-content contrasts for Buchwald–Hartwig and Ullmann reactions separate local level and fluctuation information. Negative changes reduce error; the Ullmann fluctuation contrast is near zero.

Figure_S7.title: Combining reaction scopes can require a yield sacrifice
Figure_S7.legend: **a**, Best measured route bottlenecks for two Suzuki scopes separately and after combining them on identical native support. The bracket marks the 13.48 pp yield sacrifice. **b**, Exact Pareto frontier between amide source-scope sacrifice and target-scope bottleneck. The dashed line marks 20% target yield; a source-scope sacrifice of at least 5.00 pp is required to reach it. Displayed values use two decimals; sacrifices are calculated before rounding. The routes use measured recipes.
